title: 'Where Are the Ladies?' Yash Just Answered — and All Five of Toxic's Leading Women Are About to Walk Into the Frame
excerpt: Nayanthara. Kiara Advani. Huma Qureshi. Tara Sutaria. Rukmini Vasanth. The gangster fairy tale finally shows its queens.
body:
For months, the conversation around **Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups** has been almost entirely about one man. Every teaser, every poster, every CinemaCon whisper has centred on **Yash** — the brooding KGF star, back after a two-year silence, playing a period gangster in 1940s Goa. Gorgeous? Absolutely. But fans have been asking the same question since the first promo dropped: *where are the women?*

On Monday evening, the film's official X (formerly Twitter) handle posted exactly that: "Where are the ladies?" And Yash replied with the kind of line only he can pull off:

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=JQ7pytcXahw</youtube>


> "Calm down! Ladies take time to come! Tomorrow, 01-07-2026, 11:33 AM."

Translation: a brand-new promotional asset, arriving today, will finally introduce all five of Toxic's leading women to the world. And what a lineup it is.

## The Most Stacked Female Cast in Years

Let's just name them, because the list alone makes a statement:

- **Nayanthara** — the Lady Superstar of South Indian cinema, fresh off the global run of *Jawan* with Shah Rukh Khan and currently one of the most bankable names across languages
- **Kiara Advani** — Bollywood's reigning rom-com queen, who proved she can do intensity in *Kabir Singh* and spectacle in *Satyaprem Ki Katha*
- **Huma Qureshi** — the *Gangs of Wasseypur* original, fearless and wildly underused by mainstream Bollywood, now apparently getting the showcase she deserves
- **Tara Sutaria** — trained classical singer, elegant presence, the kind of screen beauty that period cinema was made for
- **Rukmini Vasanth** — Kannada cinema's rising star, whose work in *Sapta Sagaradaache Ello* earned critical raves and cult adoration

Five women. Five distinct energies.

 One gangster universe set between the 1940s and 1970s in Goa, with Yash playing a dual-layered character named Raya. Director **Geetu Mohandas** — a National Award-winning filmmaker making her first big-canvas commercial feature — has reportedly built each woman's arc as a full character, not a decoration.

## Why the Delay Actually Worked

Toxic has had one of the most turbulent pre-release journeys in recent memory. Originally slated for March 2026, it was pushed to June, then delayed again after murmurs about reshoots sent the internet into overdrive. The makers denied the reshoot claims, but the silence around the female cast only fuelled speculation: were their roles being trimmed? Were the teasers deliberately hiding something?

If today's reveal is what insiders suggest — a dedicated promo spotlighting all five actresses — then the delay wasn't damage control. It was strategy. Hold back the women until the curiosity peaked, then deliver them all at once for maximum impact. Yash's playful "ladies take time to come" isn't just a quip; it's a flex.

## The CinemaCon Clue

Here's what we know about the film itself, based on the nine-minute preview shown at CinemaCon earlier this year that reportedly left trade attendees speechless:

- It's a **period gangster saga** set in Goa, spanning three decades (1940s–1970s)
- The makers describe it as a **"fairy tale for grown-ups"** — mythical, lush, with the kind of visual grandeur that KGF promised and then some
- **Ravi Basrur** — the composer behind KGF and *Salaar* — is handling the score, which guarantees a sonic identity that's impossible to ignore
- The film has been confirmed for **IMAX**, further cementing its big-screen ambitions
- It's releasing in **Kannada, English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam** — a true pan-India play

The locked release date is **August 26, 2026**, timed to the Onam and Raksha Bandhan holiday corridor. It won't have the weekend to itself — Shraddha Kapoor's *Eetha* and *Vvan* arrive two days later on August 28 — but Toxic's scale suggests it's playing in a different league.

## For the Diaspora

Yash's global appeal was proven definitively by KGF Chapter 2, which earned over ₹1,200 crore worldwide and became a cultural event in overseas markets. Toxic is being positioned with the same ambition: the IMAX certification, the multilingual release, and the CinemaCon unveiling all signal a film that's aiming at international screens from day one.

For NRIs in the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf, the key detail is the pan-language release — whether you watch in Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, or Telugu, it'll be the same theatrical experience, not a dubbed afterthought.

## What to Watch For

Today's reveal at 11:33 AM IST is expected to finally put faces to the roles fans have been speculating about. If Geetu Mohandas has done what the whispers suggest — built five women who are as textured and dangerous as the world they inhabit — then Toxic might just deliver something Indian cinema rarely does: a blockbuster where the women aren't playing second fiddle to the star. They're playing the whole orchestra.

Yash said the ladies take time to come. Today, they arrive.
